page: Microsoft Azure M128ls_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance engineered for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. Powered by an Intel x86_64 processor and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, the instance provides 128 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 1944.0 GB of system RAM, yielding approximately 15.19 GB of memory per vCPU.

Storage and acceleration configurations for the M128ls_v4 emphasize external persistence and CPU-driven execution. The instance includes no local storage disks and provides zero hardware GPU accelerators. Storage architecture relies entirely on network-attached Premium Storage capabilities, requiring attached remote storage for operating systems and persistent data. Additionally, complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

From an operational and resource allocation perspective, the M128ls_v4 provides extreme memory density on a single node. Deployments requiring terabyte-scale in-memory capacity benefit from running large datasets in unified memory rather than managing distributed network overhead across multiple smaller nodes. The instance is suited for enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale caching engines, SAP HANA installations, and high-memory analytics processing.
description: Microsoft Azure M128ls_v4 is a memory-optimized cloud instance within the MSMediumMemoryv4 family designed for memory-intensive enterprise applications. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 128 dedicated vCPUs using an Intel x86_64 processor architecture alongside 1944.0 GB of memory, establishing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of roughly 15.19 GB per core. The instance features no integrated local storage or hardware GPU accelerators, utilizing external Premium Storage connectivity for persistent disk workloads. Without local ephemeral storage or bundled complimentary public IPv4 addresses, the configuration is tailored for enterprise-grade network architectures and centralized storage solutions. This dense single-node footprint offers qualitative infrastructure efficiency for large in-memory databases, massive enterprise transaction systems, in-memory analytics engines, and large-scale caching deployments that demand vast RAM allocations without distributed node overhead.
